title: Spider-Man and The Odyssey are splitting up IMAX screens after a record-breaking weekend
summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey led the biggest box office weekend in history. Spider-Man's $355 million opening is the second-largest debut since Avengers: Endgame, and it will now share IMAX screens with The Odyssey starting August 6th.
content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is joining The Odyssey in IMAX theaters after both movies led the biggest weekend in box office history. On Monday, IMAX announced that Spider-Man: Brand New Day will be available in select digital IMAX locations across North America starting Thursday, August 6th.
The news comes as The Odyssey's exclusive three-weekend run in IMAX theaters comes to an end, allowing Spider-Man: Brand New Day to play alongside it, as reported by Variety. title: Samsung’s 2TB 9100 Pro SSD is actually somewhat reasonably priced
summary: Samsung's 2TB 9100 Pro SSD is available for $302.99 on Amazon, roughly $100 less than usual. As Samsung's first PCIe Gen 5 drive, it offers double the speeds of its predecessor at a competitive price point for high-capacity storage.
content:
Next to buying RAM, finding a fast, high-capacity NVMe SSD at a reasonable price has been a challenge during RAMageddon. I don’t want to say it’s getting easier, but one of Samsung’s latest SSDs is cheaper than it has sold for since February 2026. That’s something, right? Amazon has the heatsink-less version of the Samsung 9100 Pro with 2TB of storage for $302.99, which is about $100 less than the usual price. Granted, it sold for a low of $169.99 back in October 2025, but it’s a smart purchase right now compared to buying the 1TB model for $250.
Samsung 9100 Pro NVMe SSD

Where to Buy:

 $500 $302.99 at Amazon (2TB, no heatsink)
 $500 $399.99 at Best Buy (2TB no heatsink)

The 9100 Pro is Samsung’s first SSD to support PCIe Gen 5, making it a great fit if you have the right motherboard and other parts to get as much speed from it as possible. Its theoretical maximum random read and write speeds are at least twice as fast as the 990 Pro SSD that it replaced. However, it’s good (albeit slower than advertised) in a PCIe Gen 4 setup, as well. 
It’ll work fine without a heatsink in a PC or laptop (though, it’s never a bad idea to use one that fits in your system). However, you’ll need to install a heatsink in order to use this in a PlayStation 5, due to potential heat issues that could damage the SSD if used without one. Thankfully, heatsinks are super affordable, and come in a range of designs and price points.
Other great Verge-approved deals
Another Samsung-made product made the cut for today’s roundup. Its Smart Monitor lineup is worth considering if you want a PC monitor that can double as a TV, as well as a screen that you can do video chats on. Its 32-inch M8 4K monitor just hits its lowest price at Amazon and B&H Photo, selling for $349.99 — exactly 50 percent off its original $699.99 price that it hasn’t sold for since the turn of the year. content:
Leaked images of the laptop show Googlebook branding below the keyboard. | Image: Digital Citizen

title: Big Walk is like co-op Breath of the Wild
summary: Big Walk, the next game from Untitled Goose Game developer House House, shifts to cooperative multiplayer gameplay where players explore an island and solve puzzles together rather than playing as a mischievous goose.
content:
Untitled Goose Game is a tough act to follow. It was a silly experience that captured what I imagine it would feel like to be a sentient goose: a lot of waddling, a lot of honking, and a lot of shenanigans. That's why Big Walk, the next game from Goose Game developer House House, feels like a radical and unexpected departure. Instead of playing as a goose terrorizing a small village, Big Walk is a co-op multiplayer game where you explore a large island and have to work together to solve puzzles. title: China’s Alibaba takes another swipe at America’s AI supremacy
summary: Chinese tech giant Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Max, claiming it rivals leading U.S. AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI. The release heightens competitive tensions in the global AI arms race.
content:
The Alibaba logo is displayed outside its headquarters in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China. | Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images	

Chinese tech giant Alibaba released what it says is its largest and "most capable AI model to date," claiming performance rivaling the best systems from US frontier labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as domestic rivals like Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.  Alibaba said it was making the model, Qwen3.8-Max, widely available to users in a blog post published on Monday. The release had been expected after the company previewed the model last month, when it claimed it was "second only to Fable 5," Anthropic's flagship.
